saw.short: Karl Bushby finishes his 28-year walk home to Hull
saw.headline: Karl Bushby *finishes his 28-year walk* home to Hull
saw.what: Karl Bushby, 57, walked into Hull on Monday, 28 years and a day after setting off from Chile, an estimated 75 million steps with no motorised transport, per CBS. He swam the Channel last month on the way. On arrival he said: “the biggest team: Earth”.
saw.why: A very long journey with a clear finish line. People love watching someone arrive.

saw.short: Aldi's Kevin the Carrot teaser: Cauli Dog is missing
saw.headline: Aldi's Kevin the Carrot teaser: *Cauli Dog is missing*
saw.what: Aldi released a 10-second Christmas teaser in which Kevin and his daughter Chantenay put up “LOST” posters for Cauli Dog, who “stole the nation's hearts last Christmas”. Aldi says the rest of the story is “firmly under wraps”. The full ad has no release date yet.
saw.why: A mystery teaser builds the audience before the reveal. The missing posters invite guesses.

saw.short: Which? names £1.99 Aldi and Lidl Yorkshire puddings joint best
saw.headline: Which? names *£1.99 Yorkshire puddings* joint best
saw.what: In Which?'s blind test with 69 tasters, Aldi's Specially Selected Large Beef Dripping (£1.99 for 290g) and Lidl's Deluxe (£1.99 for 288g) tied top at 76%, and both are Best Buys. Aldi's are in-store only.
saw.why: Own-brand beating the famous name is catnip for debate, and roast season is here.

saw.short: A man with a Tesco Clubcard tattoo says he can't afford Tesco now
saw.headline: A man with a *Tesco Clubcard tattoo* says he can't afford Tesco now
saw.what: Dean Mayhew, 34, from Bideford, had his Clubcard QR code tattooed in July 2022. He tells Metro he can't afford Tesco now: about £200 for a midweek shop for his family. Metro notes Which? price comparisons have found Asda cheaper than Tesco, though Which?'s comparisons vary.
saw.why: Loyalty schemes meet cost-of-living pressure in a single image. Quirky stories like this travel on Facebook and TikTok.

platform.short: Reddit tests ads in search results
platform.headline: Reddit tests *ads in search results*
platform.what: Reddit is testing ads in in-app search results, targeted by the search query and carrying a small ad marker. It's starting with “a select group of eligible advertisers”. Reddit says search results have “high purchase and search intent”. No regions are given.
platform.why: Reddit is selling search intent. Worth watching if your clients use Reddit.

platform.short: TikTok adds a brand safety centre and brand protection tools
platform.headline: TikTok adds a *brand safety centre* and protection tools
platform.what: TikTok has launched a brand safety centre website, a Brand Protection Playbook and an AI Safety Essentials overview. New tools include a brand perception insights tool, copyright and trademark reporting and counterfeit protections for sellers. They were announced at a forum in Singapore, and UK availability isn't stated.
platform.why: Brand safety is a standing client question. Ask TikTok which tools apply in the UK.

platform.short: Pinterest reports 661 million monthly users in Q3
platform.headline: Pinterest reports *661 million monthly users* in Q3
platform.what: Pinterest's Q3 results, filed on 29 Oct, show 661 million monthly active users, up 10% on a year ago. Europe grew 7% to 161 million, and revenue rose 12% to $1.17bn.
platform.why: Pinterest keeps growing, and Europe is growing with it. A shopping-planning platform before Christmas.
